newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Belo says new diocese not to divide East Timorese.
newsitem.headline: Belo says new diocese not to divide East Timorese.

text.p: East Timor's outspoken Bishop Carlos Belo said the creation of a new diocese in the mostly Roman Catholic territory would not split the East Timorese, Indonesia's official Antara news agency reported on Sunday.

"The division in East Timor diocese does not mean to divide the East Timorese... on the other hand it means to improve the faith of the local people," Belo was quoted as saying in Dili, capital of East Timor, on Saturday night.
Belo was not available for comment on Sunday.

Belo was speaking at a ceremony welcoming Bishop Basilio Do Nascimento who will be the apostolic adminstrator of the newly created diocese of Baucau covering the territory's eastern half, Antara said.
Nascimento, a native East Timorese, assumes his duties this month after being chosen by Pope John Paul late last year. He will be inaugurated in Baucau on Wednesday.
Belo said the creation of the new diocese would not divide East Timor into two groups. Antara gave no further details.
East Timor previously had only one diocese, led by Nobel laureate Belo. He remains leader of the diocese based in Dili.
Nascimento was quoted by Antara as saying he was ready to fullfil his job.
"Even though it is a tough job, I will do it in the best way possible," he said.
Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in December 1975 and annexed it the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.

Belo, an immensely popular figure in the territory, was jointly awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize with self-exiled East Timorese independence advocate Jose Ramos Horta. Belo has a long-standing record of speaking out against Indonesia's sometimes harsh rule in East Timor.
